result.markdown: --- title: "Interventions and optimization" course-unit: ch11-interventions-and-optimization status: complete --- ## Scenario first, optimization second An intervention analysis has two auditable layers: 1. specify a policy and simulate it; 2. compare admissible policies with an explicit objective and constraints. The baseline is the course SIR model. A 50% transmission reduction lasts $d=10$ time units; only its start $t_1\in[0,25]$ is optimized. ::: {.notes} Separating these layers prevents an optimizer from hiding an implementation error or an implicit policy assumption. ::: ## Controlled SIR equations Add cumulative incidence $C$ and a rectangular control: $$ \begin{aligned} \dot S&=-\beta c(1-v(t))SI/N,\\ \dot I&=\beta c(1-v(t))SI/N-\gamma I,\\ \dot R&=\gamma I,\\ \dot C&=\beta c(1-v(t))SI/N, \end{aligned} $$ $$ v(t;t_1)= \begin{cases} v_{\max},&t_1\le t ``` A callback-defined policy compared with no intervention. ::: ::: ::: {.notes} `PresetTimeCallback` changes the parameter at two known times. It implements the scenario; it does not search over policies. ::: ## Bounded timing optimization ```julia function final_incidence(x, _) Array(scenario11(x[1]))[4, end] end objective = OptimizationFunction(final_incidence, AutoFiniteDiff()) problem = OptimizationProblem(objective, [8.0], nothing; lb = [0.0], ub = [25.0]) solution = solve(problem, Fminbox(LBFGS()); maxiters = 30) ``` The API makes the decision variable, objective, and box explicit. A grid is a diagnostic for the optimizer, not a substitute for stating the problem. ::: {#cell-fig-slide-ch11-objective .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#fig-slide-ch11-objective .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Final cumulative incidence across admissible intervention starts. ::: ::: ::: {.notes} Optimization can return a continuous timing estimate, while the grid reveals whether the objective is flat or has multiple plausible starts. ::: ## Validation, interpretation, and limits For every solved policy check $$ \max_t|S(t)+I(t)+R(t)-N|<10^{-6},\qquad \Delta C(t)\ge 0. $$ - The “optimal” result is conditional on reduction, duration, horizon, and cost. - Instantaneous switching, perfect adherence, homogeneous mixing, and a closed population are idealizations. - Add intervention cost, capacity, equity, uncertainty, or a peak-infection penalty when those are decision requirements. See the [book chapter](../../chapters/11-interventions-and-optimization.html), [DiffEqCallbacks.jl](https://docs.sciml.ai/DiffEqCallbacks/stable/), and [Optimization.jl](https://docs.sciml.ai/Optimization/stable/). ::: {.notes} The model is useful for learning how to formulate a decision, not for issuing a universal policy recommendation. Advanced continuous controls are deferred to the optimal-control appendix. :::
